## Pre-Difficulty Gate Failed

Difficulty not run: the submission did not pass every blocking quality or quality panel check. Oracle/NOP already passed. No Opus, GPT, analysis, or rubric-generation runs were started.

QUALITY PANEL: NEEDS REVISION -- 64 blocking issues to fix. Details for each are below.

Blocking (fix every one):
   1. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The shown corpus does not distinguish support for every
      non-repeated print-suffix combination from support for at most two suffix letters.
      (confirmed by running the grader)
   2. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The shown initial-file fixtures do not test loading a
      contract-legal file beyond a plausible fixed 32-line buffer.  (confirmed by running the
      grader)
   3. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: No visible case distinguishes literal unescaped braces in a basic
      regular expression from Python regex quantifier syntax.  (confirmed by running the grader)
   4. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The `f` command prints the default filename even when
      its FILE parameter sets, rather than requests printing of, that filename.
   5. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Looking up a mark that has never been set resolves its
      absent node to address zero instead of failing.
   6. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The basic-RE parser rejects a leading escaped
      interval, although the manual defines it as a literal expression.
   7. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Global substitution searches a sliced remainder as a
      new line, causing word-start assertions to match inside an existing word.
   8. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: A singleton join clears the undo stack despite being
      specified to do nothing.
   9. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: An unset mark is incorrectly resolved as address zero
      when the buffer is empty.
  10. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The bracket parser interprets a hyphen in first
      position as the lower endpoint of a range.
  11. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: In extended-regexp mode, the parser makes `^` and `$`
      anchors even when they occur where the contract requires literal characters.
  12. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The basic-regexp parser rejects an interval escape at
      the beginning of an expression instead of interpreting it literally.
  13. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: An unset mark resolves to address zero in an empty
      buffer, allowing an addressed append that should fail.
  14. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The move-command validation uses an exclusive upper
      bound, accepting the last moved line as its own destination despite the manual’s
      prohibition on destinations within the moved range.
  15. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Substitution yanks the deleted, pre-substitution line
      and never replaces the cut-buffer contents with the last modified line.
  16. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: A substitution without a final delimiter in a nonfinal
      global command list scans indefinitely beyond its command buffer rather than failing.
  17. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The ERE parser treats ^ as a beginning-of-line anchor
      at every position, although a mid-expression ERE ^ is literal in GNU/POSIX syntax.
  18. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The extended-regexp parser treats ^ as a
      beginning-of-line anchor at every ERE position, rather than a literal when it follows an
      ordinary atom.
  19. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: A nonexistent mark is accepted as address zero when
      the line buffer is empty, permitting put from a retained cut buffer instead of failing the
      mark address.
  20. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The BRE parser always treats a leading escaped left
      brace as an invalid repetition rather than the literal interval-looking text required when
      that form occurs first in a RE or subexpression.
  21. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: A global command clears the undo stack even when its
      pattern selected no line, so it prevents undoing the preceding modifying command.
  22. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: The global command-list continuation parser accepts a
      backslash-only first list line, thereby inventing a leading blank command instead of
      rejecting a list whose required first command is not on the g line (or is not a command in
      a G list).
  23. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: An empty i command leaves current at the line before
      the addressed line rather than at its addressed line.
  24. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR: Deleting or substituting a marked line does not clear
      its mark, so undo can resurrect a mark that the contract requires to have been cleared by
      modification.
  25. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The package audit rejects contract-legal binary supporting data,
      applying a text-only artifact policy broader than the pure-Python and standard-library
      restrictions.
  26. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The visible offset cases do not require the parser to accept
      whitespace between successive signed offsets.
  27. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The visible boundary cases do not isolate rejection of a final
      negative address.
  28. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The visible corpus never tests that '-' is literal in the final
      position of a bracket class.
  29. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The visible `[:cntrl:]` test has no matching control character,
      allowing a parser that implements this class as empty.
  30. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The shown backreference cases never require a third or higher
      numbered capture, although the contract requires references through nine.
  31. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The visible cases exercise repetitions after atoms but do not
      require quantifier-looking syntax to become literal at the start of an expression or
      subexpression.
  32. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The shown `\w` case does not require underscore to count as a word
      character.
  33. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The shown cases reject nested g, G, and v, but do not reject
      nested V.
  34. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: Only append demonstrates omission of a final input-mode terminator
      in a global list; change and insert do not.
  35. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The shown interactive G cases do not exercise a
      backslash-continued command list.
  36. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The shown undo cases enforce whole-command undo for g, but not for
      G, v, or V.
  37. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The shown write cases do not decisively check that w and W
      preserve current address when the written range ends elsewhere.
  38. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: Checking current after a split and checking the cut buffer after
      an unsplit substitution does not check which split result enters the cut buffer.
  39. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: One alternate s delimiter does not enforce the documented choice
      of any permitted delimiter.
  40. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: Replacement backreferences above `\2` are not exercised, despite
      the required range extending through `\9`.
  41. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The visible global-undo case leaves only one matching line, so it
      cannot reject executing a global command list containing `u` more than once.
  42. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The visible verifier omits malformed accepted-option layouts
      required by the CLI contract: accepted options after FILE and -p without its required
      following string.
  43. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The visible cases test '*' after a character and as a leading
      literal, but not '*' applied to a parenthesized basic subexpression.
  44. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The visible corpus omits the required literal interpretation of a
      bounded-repeat token when it begins an RE or subexpression.
  45. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The visible corpus does not distinguish a print suffix immediately
      adjacent to its command from a permissive parser that accepts whitespace before it.
  46. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The shown verifier lacks a case that rejects an omitted final
      substitute delimiter when that substitute is not the final command of a continued g/v
      command list.
  47. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The verifier tests omitted final substitution delimiters only when
      the substitution is the final command, not the required rejection of an omitted delimiter
      before another command in a g/v command list.
  48. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: No visible case checks that a replacement backslash escaping
      another backslash yields one literal backslash.
  49. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The repeat-substitution tests omit COUNT and p suffix behavior,
      including toggling a saved print suffix.
  50. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The corpus has no NUL-containing fixture, so binary newline
      preservation and the modified-binary/read-empty-file exception are never tested.
  51. [Correct Reference Solution] MINOR: The option parser accepts option spellings the
      contract excludes, including combined flags, attached -p strings, and -G/-v.
  52. [Correct Reference Solution] MINOR: A substitution without its final delimiter inside a
      nonfinal g/v command list is accepted by swallowing the following command-list text as
      replacement text instead of being rejected.
  53. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The runtime import guard classifies site-packages beneath the
      Python standard-library directory as standard-library code.
  54. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: No shown case directly distinguishes y preserving current from y
      setting current to the last yanked line.
  55. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The shown cut-buffer cases never distinguish replacement by a
      second y from retaining or accumulating the first yank.
  56. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The shown comment checks require an address, leaving address-free
      comments unexercised.
  57. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: No shown case checks a numeric COUNT on the repeat-substitution
      form.
  58. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The shown `sg` case does not test the required reset of a previous
      numeric COUNT.
  59. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The shown repeat-substitution examples never observe whether `sp`
      toggles an existing print suffix off.
  60. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The shown `sr` case tests a later search but not the condition
      that the search must follow the substitution.
  61. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The visible corpus lacks cases for raw BRE brace/angle literals
      and for a general ordinary escaped literal, leaving a BRE translator that delegates those
      forms to Python regex behavior insufficiently checked.
  62. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The visible corpus does not test rejection of a nonblank first g
      COMMAND-LIST command deferred to the next physical line.
  63. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: No visible global-command case establishes that file commands such
      as w remain legal members of a g COMMAND-LIST.
  64. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The visible interactive-global cases never apply an explicit
      address range to G, leaving its required address scoping unexercised.

Checked and clean: Coherent Contract, Protected Ground Truth, Deterministic Execution.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DETAILS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The shown corpus does not distinguish support for every non-repeated print-suffix combination
   from support for at most two suffix letters.
   Confirmed by running the grader: a broken submission still passed after this change --
   "Replaces the print-suffix parser so that it accepts no more than two distinct suffix
   letters" (reference reward 1.0, changed 1.0).
   Why this fails:
     Reach: On a contract-legal one-line file containing `a\n`, send `1pln\n`. GNU ed combines
     all three suffix effects. Flip: A plausible parser that accepts one or two print suffixes
     but rejects three would match the shown `1pn` and `2ln` cases, yet emit `?\n` instead of
     the GNU result for this input. The verifier compares exact output, but no shown suffix case
     supplies three letters. This conclusion is limited to the shown files; mixed_scripts_6–8
     were NOT SHOWN.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:590-595, tests/cases/print_list_number.jsonl:8-9,
     tests/test_outputs.py:133-143

2. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The shown initial-file fixtures do not test loading a contract-legal file beyond a plausible
   fixed 32-line buffer.
   Confirmed by running the grader: a broken submission still passed after this change --
   "Replaces initial command-line file loading with a 32-line-limited load while leaving later
   read commands unlimited" (reference reward 1.0, changed 1.0).
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Supply an ASCII FILE of 33 short, newline-terminated lines and the script `33p\n`.
     Thirty-three lines is within a few dozen. Flip: An implementation with a 32-line limit
     specifically when initially reading FILE can pass the shown initial fixtures, whose largest
     files have 24 lines, but cannot print line 33 correctly. Applying the cap only at initial
     load means later edits do not distinguish it. The fixture table is fixed by load_cases; the
     three NOT SHOWN mixed-script files could not be inspected.
   Where to look: instruction.md:10, tests/cases/fixtures.json:2-12, tests/test_outputs.py:27-57

3. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   No visible case distinguishes literal unescaped braces in a basic regular expression from
   Python regex quantifier syntax.
   Confirmed by running the grader: a broken submission still passed after this change --
   "Replaces basic-regexp parsing so an unescaped opening brace is rejected rather than treated
   as a literal" (reference reward 1.0, changed 1.0).
   Why this fails:
     Reach: With an empty directory, script `a\n{2}\n.\ng/{2}/p\nQ\n` is contract-legal; GNU ed
     treats `{2}` literally and prints `{2}\n`. Flip: A plausible basic-RE translator converts
     escaped `\{2\}` into quantifier syntax but leaves unescaped `{2}` unchanged for Python
     `re`, which rejects it and emits `?`. It passes the shown escaped-brace operator cases and
     literal-parenthesis case, but would fail this comparison.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:460-465, tests/cases/regex.jsonl:12,
     tests/cases/regex.jsonl:33, tests/cases/regex.jsonl:40, tests/test_outputs.py:132-143

4. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR
   The `f` command prints the default filename even when its FILE parameter sets, rather than
   requests printing of, that filename.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Feed `f foo\nQ\n` with no initial FILE. The manual says `f FILE` sets the filename
     and prints it only when FILE is omitted. Flip: GNU ed produces no stdout; the reference
     assigns `foo` and unconditionally emits `foo\n`.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:651-653, solution/pyed/ed.py:1131-1139

5. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR
   Looking up a mark that has never been set resolves its absent node to address zero instead of
   failing.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Feed `'a=\nQ\n` without setting mark a. `get_line_node_addr(None)` walks back to the
     list head and returns zero; `=` accepts and prints that address. Flip: GNU ed reports an
     invalid marked address with `?\n`, whereas the reference prints `0\n`.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:409-412, solution/pyed/ed.py:164-175,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:891-896, solution/pyed/ed.py:1296-1299

6. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR
   The basic-RE parser rejects a leading escaped interval, although the manual defines it as a
   literal expression.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Use regular-file standard input containing `a\n{2}\n.\ns/\\{2\\}/ok/\nw
     target\nQ\n`, with no initial FILE. The manual explicitly says a leading `\{2\}` matches
     literal `{2}`, so GNU ed substitutes `ok`, writes `target` containing `ok\n`, and exits
     zero. Flip: the reference raises a regex error at the leading `\{`, prints `?\n`, stops
     before `w`, leaves `target` unwritten, and exits nonzero.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:527-536, solution/pyed/posixre.py:137-143,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:421-426, solution/pyed/ed.py:1374-1387

7. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR -- core domain and business logic
   Global substitution searches a sliced remainder as a new line, causing word-start assertions
   to match inside an existing word.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: With piped stdin, submit `a\nab\n.\ns/\\<./X/g\n,p\nQ\n`. The manual defines `\\<`
     as a word-beginning anchor. On the original line `ab`, only `a` begins a word, so
     substitution must leave `Xb`, which `,p` must print. Flip: the reference first replaces
     `a`, then sets `txt` to `b` at ed.py:612 and searches it at line 621. posixre.py:335-340
     sees no character before `b`, treats it as another word beginning, and replaces it too. The
     reference therefore prints `XX` instead of `Xb`.
   Where to look: instruction.md:7-8, environment/app/docs/ed.txt:544-549,
     environment/app/docs/ed.txt:870-880, solution/pyed/ed.py:593-626,
     solution/pyed/posixre.py:335-340

8. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR
   A singleton join clears the undo stack despite being specified to do nothing.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Start with an existing ASCII file containing `base\n`, supply standard input through
     a pipe, and run `a\nnew\n.\n1j\nu\n,p\nQ\n`. The append makes `new` the last undoable
     modification. The explicit `1j` has equal endpoints and, by the manual, does nothing. Flip:
     The reference nevertheless calls clear_undo_stack before its `first_addr < second_addr`
     test. Its `u` reports `?`, and `,p` prints both `base` and `new`; the required undo removes
     `new`, so `,p` prints only `base`. The failure also changes the exit-status decision.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:709-714, environment/app/docs/ed.txt:780-785,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:1167-1173, solution/pyed/ed.py:365-369

9. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR
   An unset mark is incorrectly resolved as address zero when the buffer is empty.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Start with no FILE and an empty buffer, using pipe input containing `'a=\nQ\n`. No k
     command has marked a line, so the contract's `'a` address is invalid and GNU ed reports an
     error. In get_line_node_addr(None), the empty circular list returns to its head before
     incrementing addr, and the function returns 0 rather than -1. The = command then prints
     `0\n`. Flip: the reference produces `0\n` and exits zero after Q, instead of producing the
     command-error `?\n` and a nonzero status.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:409-412, environment/app/docs/ed.txt:858-860,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:164-175, solution/pyed/ed.py:891-896, solution/pyed/ed.py:1296-1299

10. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR
   The bracket parser interprets a hyphen in first position as the lower endpoint of a range.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: With a pipe as stdin, run `a\n0\n.\n1s/[-a]/X/p\nQ\n`. The documented first-position
     rule makes `[-a]` contain only `-` and `a`, so GNU ed reports the failed substitution with
     `?\n`. Flip: the reference consumes `-` and `a` as endpoints, includes `0` in the resulting
     range, and emits `X\n` instead.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:474-487, solution/pyed/posixre.py:240-249

11. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR
   In extended-regexp mode, the parser makes `^` and `$` anchors even when they occur where the
   contract requires literal characters.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Run with `-E` and piped stdin `a\na^b\n.\n1s/a^b/X/p\nQ\n`. The middle `^` is
     literal under the stated position rule, so the substitution prints `X\n`. Flip: the
     reference constructs a beginning-of-line anchor after matching `a`; that cannot match
     there, so it prints `?\n`. Its unconditional extended-mode `$` branch has the corresponding
     middle-position problem.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:500-507, solution/pyed/posixre.py:153-168

12. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR
   The basic-regexp parser rejects an interval escape at the beginning of an expression instead
   of interpreting it literally.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: With piped stdin, run `a\n{2}\n.\n1s/\\{2\\}/X/p\nQ\n`. The documented
     initial-position exception makes `\\{2\\}` match literal `{2}`, so the substitution prints
     `X\n`. Flip: `atom()` immediately raises `RegexError` on the initial `\\{`, producing `?\n`
     and leaving the line unchanged.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:527-536, solution/pyed/posixre.py:137-143,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:420-428

13. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR
   An unset mark resolves to address zero in an empty buffer, allowing an addressed append that
   should fail.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Start without FILE and provide regular-file stdin containing `'aa\nnew\n.\n,p\nQ\n`.
     No line has been marked `a`. The quoted address lookup passes `None` to
     `get_line_node_addr`; with an empty list its first traversal immediately returns to the
     head, so `addr` remains zero and the function returns zero. `a` then accepts that address
     and inserts `new`. Flip: GNU ed must reject the unset marked-line address, print `?\n`, and
     stop on regular-file stdin with nonzero status. The reference instead executes the append
     and subsequently prints `new\n` for `,p`, reaching `Q` with zero status.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:409-412, instruction.md:10,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:164-175, solution/pyed/ed.py:891-896, solution/pyed/ed.py:1091-1097

14. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR
   The move-command validation uses an exclusive upper bound, accepting the last moved line as
   its own destination despite the manual’s prohibition on destinations within the moved range.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: With pipe stdin, run `a\none\ntwo\n.\n1,2m2\n,p\nQ\n`. The destination 2 is within
     the moved range 1–2, so the contract requires that command to fail and emit `?\n`; the pipe
     then permits `,p`, yielding `?\none\ntwo\n` and a nonzero exit status. Flip: The reference
     evaluates `1 <= 2 < 2` as false, enters move_lines’ `addr == second` no-op branch, and
     emits only `one\ntwo\n`; Q then exits with status zero.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:729-735, solution/pyed/ed.py:1192-1205,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:320-326

15. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR
   Substitution yanks the deleted, pre-substitution line and never replaces the cut-buffer
   contents with the last modified line.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: On pipe input `a\na\n.\ns/a/b/\n0x\n,p\nQ\n`, substitution changes the sole `a` to
     `b`. The contract requires its last modified line, `b`, in the cut buffer, so `0x` followed
     by `,p` must print `b\nb\n`. In the reference, search_and_replace calls delete_lines, whose
     yank_lines copies `a`, then inserts `b` without updating the cut buffer. Flip: `0x` inserts
     `a`, so `,p` prints `a\nb\n` instead.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:818-826, environment/app/docs/ed.txt:897-902,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:293-304, solution/pyed/ed.py:637-645

16. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR
   A substitution without a final delimiter in a nonfinal global command list scans indefinitely
   beyond its command buffer rather than failing.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: With pipe input `a\na\n.\ng/a/s/a/b\\\np\nQ\n`, the continued global list has
     `s/a/b` followed by a separate `p` command. The manual forbids omitting the substitution's
     final delimiter when that substitution is nonfinal. The reference joins the continued list,
     then extract_replacement consumes its newline and `p`; at buffer end Cmd.ch returns `\0`,
     but the loop continues looking for `/` and repeatedly appends `\0`. Flip: GNU ed's command
     error produces `?\n` and continues on pipe input; the reference does not reach that error
     or the subsequent `Q`.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:904-910, solution/pyed/ed.py:52-54,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:545-561, solution/pyed/ed.py:1313-1321

17. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR -- core domain and business logic
   The ERE parser treats ^ as a beginning-of-line anchor at every position, although a
   mid-expression ERE ^ is literal in GNU/POSIX syntax.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: create ASCII file f containing `a^b\n` and run the valid pipe script
     `1s/a^b/X/p\nQ\n` as `python3 /app/pyed/ed.py -E f`. Flip: GNU ed treats the ^ in `a^b`
     literally, substitutes, prints `X\n`, and exits zero (after its initial `4\n` read count).
     Parser.atom consumes `a`, then at ^ takes the `if self.ere or start` branch and creates
     bol, so the reference cannot match after a; command_s reports no match, main_loop emits
     `?\n`, and exits nonzero. This changes both required stdout and exit status.
   Where to look: instruction.md:1-8, environment/app/docs/ed.txt:500-507,
     solution/pyed/posixre.py:153-175, solution/pyed/ed.py:1053-1081,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:1374-1387

18. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR -- core domain and business logic
   The extended-regexp parser treats ^ as a beginning-of-line anchor at every ERE position,
   rather than a literal when it follows an ordinary atom.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: invoke `ed.py -E` with pipe input `a\na^b\n.\ns/a^b/X/\np\nQ\n`. The buffer line is
     `a^b`; GNU ERE interprets the non-initial ^ literally, so substitution succeeds and p emits
     `X` with zero exit status. Flip: Parser.atom sees ^ after parsing `a` but lines 153-160 use
     `if self.ere or start`, producing a bol node; `a` followed by bol cannot match. The
     substitution emits `?`, p emits `a^b`, and the non-loose exit status is bad.
   Where to look: instruction.md:5-8, environment/app/docs/ed.txt:275-278,
     solution/pyed/posixre.py:153-160, solution/pyed/ed.py:998-1081

19. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR -- core domain and business logic
   A nonexistent mark is accepted as address zero when the line buffer is empty, permitting put
   from a retained cut buffer instead of failing the mark address.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: pipe `a\none\n.\n1d\n'ax\n1p\nQ\n`. Deletion leaves an empty buffer but preserves
     yank=`one`; no k command has set mark a. The contract permits apostrophe addresses only for
     a line previously marked, so GNU must issue `?` for `'ax`; the following `1p` also errors
     because the buffer remains empty. Flip: get_marked_node_addr calls
     get_line_node_addr(None); on an empty list it returns 0 (the `if addr` error guard is
     false). x explicitly accepts 0 and put_lines restores the retained `one`, so `1p` prints
     `one` and the reference exits successfully rather than reporting the required errors.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:716-720, environment/app/docs/ed.txt:818-821,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:164-175, solution/pyed/ed.py:891-896, solution/pyed/ed.py:1271-1279

20. [Correct Reference Solution] MAJOR -- core domain and business logic
   The BRE parser always treats a leading escaped left brace as an invalid repetition rather
   than the literal interval-looking text required when that form occurs first in a RE or
   subexpression.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: with pipe stdin, run the valid script `a\n{2}\n.\ns/\\{2\\}/X/p\nQ\n`. The manual
     expressly says a first `\\{2\\}` is literal and matches `{2}`, so GNU ed substitutes and
     prints `X\n` with zero status. Flip: Parser.atom sees the leading backslash and `{` and
     immediately raises RegexError at solution/pyed/posixre.py:140-141; compile_regex converts
     it to an invalid-RE command error, so main_loop emits `?\n` and returns nonzero. No

## Quality Check Results
✅ pass - verifiable: test_outputs.py deterministically runs GNU ed 1.19 (baked into tests/Dockerfile) and the candidate through a launcher, in fresh temp dirs, comparing stdout byte-for-byte, exit status, and resulting files. No LLM-as-judge, no runtime network installs in test.sh (all verifier tooling - pytest, pytest-json-ctrf, ed - is baked into tests/Dockerfile). The roster/fixtures self-check (load_cases) guards against silent corpus drift.
✅ pass - solvable: solution/pyed/ed.py and posixre.py provide a complete, structurally faithful port of GNU ed's C implementation (matching known internal function/variable names such as search_line_node, put_sbuf_line, u_current) plus an exhaustive leftmost-longest POSIX regex engine. solve.sh simply installs these pre-written files. Given expert_time_estimate_hours=12 and the size/fidelity of the port, this is achievable by an expert already familiar with ed's algorithm, though it is on the high end of 'a few hours'.
✅ pass - difficult: Requires precise knowledge of ed's undo/redo semantics, global-active-list bookkeeping, current-address rules after every command, POSIX BRE/ERE leftmost-longest matching (which Python's re does not implement), and error/exit-status edge cases. This goes well beyond a typical undergraduate exercise and matches the stated difficulty_explanation.
✅ pass - interesting: Reimplementing a standard POSIX utility for minimal/distroless container images is a realistic professional scenario (embedded/minimal-image maintenance, script portability); the relevant_experience field plausibly identifies the audience (Unix systems engineers maintaining ed/sed scripts).
✅ pass - outcome_verified: Tests only check final stdout, exit status, and resulting files against a live GNU ed run; instructions describe required behavior/output, not an implementation approach. No process-level constraints on how the agent must implement pyed.
✅ pass - anti_cheat_robustness: The agent image ships no ed binary and has no network at solve time (agent network_mode=no-network), preventing trivial delegation. The guard.py launcher uses sys.addaudithook and a meta_path Warden to block subprocess/exec/fork/ctypes and non-stdlib/non-delivered imports, verified against five probe programs (launcher.py, exec_launcher.py, vendored.py, native.py, plain.py). test_delivered_package_is_standard_library_python additionally scans all delivered files for binary/native content and disallowed imports via AST, closing the loophole of dropping a compiled .so under /app. Ground truth is produced live from the verifier's own root-only /usr/bin/ed, never exposed to the agent.
✅ pass - task_security: No credential access, no exfiltration, no obfuscation. The guardcheck probes intentionally attempt subprocess/exec/ctypes usage purely to test the anti-cheat guard, which is the guard's own documented purpose. One case reads /etc/hostname via ed's 'r' command, which is benign (compared identically between reference and candidate, no external transmission).
✅ pass - functional_verification: The core verification (check()) executes both GNU ed and the candidate on 1644 real command scripts and diffs stdout/exit-status/files. The only string/AST-based checks (test_delivered_package_is_standard_library_python) validate the 'stdlib-only, no native code' constraint, which cannot be checked by execution alone and is a legitimate complement, not a substitute, for behavioral testing.
✅ pass - deterministic_reproducible: Base images pinned by sha256 digest; pytest and pytest-json-ctrf pinned to exact versions; apt-get ed is intentionally left unpinned per guidance (apt mirrors only carry current point releases). No live/mutable network services are used at verify time (network_mode=no-network for both agent and verifier).
✅ pass - essential_difficulty: The byte-exact output requirement is intrinsic to faithfully cloning GNU ed's documented behavior (e.g. the 'l' command's escaping rules, diagnostic messages), not an arbitrary formatting overlay bolted onto an otherwise different task. Failures would stem from misunderstanding ed's genuine semantics (current-address rules, undo, leftmost-longest matching), not clerical precision.
✅ pass - test_instruction_alignment: Every requirement in instruction.md (options -E/-l/-p/-q/-r/-s and no others, address forms, BRE/ERE with GNU escapes, leftmost-longest matching, all other commands/suffixes/global/undo/marks/G/V, error '?' + stop-on-regular-file/continue-on-pipe behavior) is covered by a corresponding case family or the launcher/package tests. Verified absence of excluded features (h/H commands, -G/-v options, '!' usage) in the corpus, matching the instruction's stated exceptions.
✅ pass - novel: While GNU ed's source is public, reproducing its exact behavioral edge cases (POSIX leftmost-longest regex semantics that Python's re lacks, undo-of-undo, global active-list interactions) requires genuine engineering rather than recall of a memorized textbook solution; this is not a standard training-corpus exercise like FizzBuzz or sorting.
✅ pass - agentic: The scope (a ~1850-line line editor plus a custom regex engine, validated only indirectly since the agent has no local ed binary or network access to check itself) cannot be produced correctly in a single zero-shot generation; it requires iterative file editing, self-testing, and debugging over many steps.
✅ pass - reviewable: Expected outputs are not hardcoded; they are derived at verification time by running the actual GNU ed 1.19 binary, so a non-specialist reviewer can trust the oracle without independently verifying ed semantics. The verification_explanation and difficulty_explanation document the design (roster/fixture self-check, launcher probes) clearly enough for review.
✅ pass - instruction_concision: instruction.md is dense but purely descriptive of required behavior (uses absolute paths /app/pyed/ed.py, /app/docs/ed.txt; backticks for commands/paths; no headings, roleplay, or step-by-step procedure). It does not hint at implementation approach (no mention of linked lists, undo stacks, etc.).
✅ pass - solution_quality: solve.sh only copies pre-written solution/pyed/ed.py and posixre.py (each far over 20 lines) rather than inlining them as heredocs, matching the guidance to keep large files separate. The files themselves demonstrate genuine, non-trivial computation (a full editor engine and regex matcher), not a hardcoded answer.
✅ pass - separate_verifier_configured: All verifier inputs (case corpus, guard/guardcheck/guardvendor, GNU ed binary, pytest/ctrf tooling) are baked into tests/Dockerfile; nothing is read from undeclared agent-container paths. No runtime pip/apt installs occur in test.sh. There are no shared assets duplicated between environment/ and tests/ that could drift.
✅ pass - environment_hygiene: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (README, docs, pyed stub); tests/ and solution/ are excluded via .dockerignore and never copied. tests/Dockerfile installs its own test-only deps (ed, pytest, pytest-json-ctrf) at build time, not in test.sh. Apt installs in both Dockerfiles are unpinned (correct per guidance) and followed by rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* cleanup, preceded by apt-get update.
➖ not_applicable - structured_data_schema: The task's expected output is plain stdout/file content matching GNU ed's behavior, not a structured schema like JSON/CSV/API response, so no normative schema documentation is needed.
✅ pass - typos: No typos found in task-authored files (instruction.md, task.toml, solve.sh, test.sh, guard.py, test_outputs.py, case files). The single 'occurences' typo found is inside the verbatim upstream GNU ed manual text (environment/app/docs/ed.txt), not task-authored content.
✅ pass - difficulty_explanation_quality: difficulty_explanation concretely enumerates the specific hard sub-problems (current-address rules, undo-of-undo, global active-list semantics, interactive G/V, leftmost-longest POSIX matching, error/exit-status nuances) and explains why an engineer working from memory would get specific details wrong. It also clarifies the corpus is synthetically generated from the grammar rather than an external corpus, addressing the data-realism requirement. The real-world audience is covered via the closely related relevant_experience field rather than embedded verbatim in difficulty_explanation, a minor stylistic gap.
✅ pass - solution_explanation_quality: solution_explanation accurately describes the two-file approach (posixre.py for BRE/ERE parsing and exhaustive leftmost-longest matching; ed.py for the circular line-list/undo-stack port) and is fully consistent with the actual solution files inspected.
✅ pass - verification_explanation_quality: verification_explanation accurately and specifically describes the verifier's mechanics (roster/fixture self-check, live GNU ed oracle per case, root-only ed binary, unprivileged launcher-wrapped candidate run, byte-for-byte/exit-status/file comparison, five guard probes, delivered-package stdlib/text check), all of which match what was found in test_outputs.py and guard.py.
✅ pass - category_and_tags: category='Software' and subcategory='Languages' reasonably fit a task about implementing a command-language interpreter and its own regex dialect. Tags (gnu-ed, line-editor, posix-regex, undo, reimplementation) are specific and descriptive, not generic.
✅ pass - no_extraneous_files: Every file inspected is referenced by a Dockerfile, the instruction, solve.sh, or the test harness (roster.json/fixtures.json cross-checked against the *.jsonl case files and found perfectly consistent, with fixture and total counts matching exactly). No leftover, backup, or unused files were found; the only hidden file is the standard .dockerignore.
✅ pass - verifier_execution_isolation: Candidate code always runs via setpriv --reuid=65534 (nobody), never as root, and never in-process inside pytest (always via subprocess.Popen). /logs/verifier and /tests are chmod 700 and the reference ed binary is chmod 700 before any candidate code runs. Reward is derived by root (test.sh) purely from pytest's exit code. The audit-hook guard blocks fork/exec/spawn outright, closing the double-fork-daemon attack this criterion targets; timeouts kill the whole process group via killpg with start_new_session=True.
✅ pass - ctrf_reporting: test.sh invokes pytest with --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json directly against test_outputs.py, covering its 24 discrete tests (22 case-family tests plus the two guard/package tests), matching the standard CTRF pattern exactly.
➖ not_applicable - do_not_modify_enforced: instruction.md contains no 'do not modify/preserve/leave unchanged' constraint naming a concrete artifact; its behavioral constraints (stdlib-only, no subprocess, no native code) are enforced by the guard/launcher and delivered-package tests but are not 'do-not-modify-a-file' constraints in the sense this criterion targets.
✅ pass - binary_reward: test.sh writes exactly 0 initially, then unconditionally overwrites reward.txt with either '1' (rc==0) or '0' (rc!=0) based solely on pytest's exit code; every reachable path writes exactly 0 or 1, with no fractional or weighted scoring anywhere in the verifier.

novel.explanation: While the editor-state logic in solution/pyed/ed.py mirrors GNU ed's own C algorithm structure (which a model could partially recall), the load-bearing POSIX leftmost-longest regex engine in posixre.py has no analogous reusable reference inside ed's own source (ed delegates regex matching to glibc) and must be independently designed and implemented, preventing a pure memorization shortcut for a significant fraction of the test families.

typos.explanation: No typos found in filenames, paths, commands, or identifiers across instruction.md, task.toml, Dockerfiles, solve.sh, test.sh, or the Python sources (occasional spelling like 'occurences'/'mesages' appears only inside the copied verbatim GNU ed manual text, not in task-authored content).

agentic.explanation: The agent has no ed binary and no network access to obtain one, so it must read the ~1000-line manual (/app/docs/ed.txt), iteratively author and self-test a multi-file implementation, and debug subtle edge cases across many sessions/tool-calls without an oracle to compare against — this cannot be solved by a single zero-shot generation.

solvable.explanation: solution/pyed/ed.py and posixre.py provide a complete, carefully structured implementation (buffer as linked line-nodes, undo stack, active-list global commands, a from-scratch POSIX backtracking regex engine with leftmost-longest semantics) that solve.sh installs into /app/pyed. The code is coherent, internally consistent with the manual's described behavior, and the declared 12-hour expert estimate, while above a 'few hours', is a single workday for an editor+regex-engine port, not a multi-day undertaking.

difficult.explanation: The task requires precise replication of ed's stateful current-address rules, undo-of-undo semantics, global active-list tracking, and, notably, a genuine POSIX leftmost-longest regular-expression matcher, which Python's re module does not provide and which GNU ed itself delegates to glibc rather than implementing — this sub-problem cannot be solved by simply porting ed's own C source and requires real algorithmic/regex-engine expertise.

reviewable.explanation: The verifier derives expected results by executing the actual GNU ed 1.19 binary at test time rather than hardcoding expected outputs, so a non-specialist reviewer can trust the ground truth without ed expertise; task.toml's verification_explanation matches this design precisely.

verifiable.explanation: tests/test_outputs.py runs the real /usr/bin/ed (baked into tests/Dockerfile, root-only after chmod) and the candidate /app/pyed/ed.py against 250+ scripted cases in cases.json, comparing stdout byte-for-byte, exit-status zero-ness, and final directory contents. This is fully programmatic, deterministic (no LLM-as-judge, no randomness), and requires no runtime network installs (pytest/ctrf are pip-installed at image build time in tests/Dockerfile; test.sh only runs pytest).

interesting.explanation: Providing a pure-Python, dependency-free line editor for minimal/distroless container images that still rely on ed-driven maintenance scripts is a real, if niche, systems-engineering scenario (analogous to busybox/toybox utility reimplementations for constrained environments).

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh only ever writes literal `0` or `1` to /logs/verifier/reward.txt on every reachable path (initial default 0, PWD-guard failure 0, pytest success 1, pytest failure 0); no fractional or weighted scoring exists.

task_security.explanation: No credential access, external network calls, obfuscation, or destructive operations were found in environment/Dockerfile, tests/Dockerfile, test.sh, or solve.sh; the 'r /etc/hostname' and 'w ../x.txt' test cases exercise ed's own -r restricted-mode enforcement inside ephemeral tmp directories, not real host paths outside the sandbox.

essential_difficulty.explanation: The byte-exact output comparison mirrors ed's actual observable behavior (its own text formatting is the specification, not an arbitrary added format), so difficulty stems from correctly modeling address/undo/regex/global-command semantics rather than from artificial formatting or precision requirements.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: The agent's image (environment/Dockerfile) does not install the real 'ed' package and the agent has no runtime network access ([agent].network_mode = "no-network"), so it cannot obtain or shell out to a genuine ed binary to fake correctness. do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: instruction.md contains no 'do not modify/preserve/leave unchanged' constraint naming a concrete artifact; it only restricts implementation technique (stdlib-only, no subprocess), which is not a protect-an-artifact constraint.

structured_data_schema.explanation: Output is ed's own raw byte stream (plain text), not a structured data format (JSON/CSV/schema) requiring normative documentation.

functional_verification.explanation: Verification executes both the reference ed binary and the candidate script as subprocesses on real input files and diffs actual stdout/exit-status/file-state; there is no string/keyword matching against source code anywhere in the test suite.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: pytest==9.1.1 and pytest-json-ctrf==0.5.2 are version-pinned in tests/Dockerfile; the apt-installed 'ed' package is correctly left unpinned per apt conventions; no live external services are used; ed's command scripts and fixtures are static and non-random, so repeated runs should be consistent.

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: test.sh chmods /logs/verifier and /tests to 700 (root-only) before any candidate code runs; test_outputs.py executes the candidate exclusively via `setpriv --reuid=65534 --regid=65534 --clear-groups --no-new-privs` (no in-process import of agent code), captures output via communicate() with a 20s timeout and process-group SIGKILL on timeout, and root's test.sh derives the reward solely from pytest's own exit code.

difficulty_explanation_quality.explanation: The explanation concretely names the hard sub-problems (current-address tracking, undo-of-undo, global active-list semantics, interactive G/V, POSIX leftmost-longest regex vs Python's re) and states why an engineer working from memory alone gets specific details wrong; it lacks an explicit one-sentence 'who does this in real life' but the surrounding relevant_experience field and instruction context make this clear by implication.

novel.explanation: While GNU ed's source is public, reproducing its exact behavioral edge cases (POSIX leftmost-longest regex semantics that Python's re lacks, undo-of-undo, global active-list interactions) requires genuine engineering rather than recall of a memorized textbook solution; this is not a standard training-corpus exercise like FizzBuzz or sorting.

typos.explanation: No typos found in task-authored files (instruction.md, task.toml, solve.sh, test.sh, guard.py, test_outputs.py, case files). The single 'occurences' typo found is inside the verbatim upstream GNU ed manual text (environment/app/docs/ed.txt), not task-authored content.

agentic.explanation: The scope (a ~1850-line line editor plus a custom regex engine, validated only indirectly since the agent has no local ed binary or network access to check itself) cannot be produced correctly in a single zero-shot generation; it requires iterative file editing, self-testing, and debugging over many steps.

solvable.explanation: solution/pyed/ed.py and posixre.py provide a complete, structurally faithful port of GNU ed's C implementation (matching known internal function/variable names such as search_line_node, put_sbuf_line, u_current) plus an exhaustive leftmost-longest POSIX regex engine. solve.sh simply installs these pre-written files. Given expert_time_estimate_hours=12 and the size/fidelity of the port, this is achievable by an expert already familiar with ed's algorithm, though it is on the high end of 'a few hours'.

difficult.explanation: Requires precise knowledge of ed's undo/redo semantics, global-active-list bookkeeping, current-address rules after every command, POSIX BRE/ERE leftmost-longest matching (which Python's re does not implement), and error/exit-status edge cases. This goes well beyond a typical undergraduate exercise and matches the stated difficulty_explanation.

reviewable.explanation: Expected outputs are not hardcoded; they are derived at verification time by running the actual GNU ed 1.19 binary, so a non-specialist reviewer can trust the oracle without independently verifying ed semantics. The verification_explanation and difficulty_explanation document the design (roster/fixture self-check, launcher probes) clearly enough for review.

verifiable.explanation: test_outputs.py deterministically runs GNU ed 1.19 (baked into tests/Dockerfile) and the candidate through a launcher, in fresh temp dirs, comparing stdout byte-for-byte, exit status, and resulting files. No LLM-as-judge, no runtime network installs in test.sh (all verifier tooling - pytest, pytest-json-ctrf, ed - is baked into tests/Dockerfile). The roster/fixtures self-check (load_cases) guards against silent corpus drift.

interesting.explanation: Reimplementing a standard POSIX utility for minimal/distroless container images is a realistic professional scenario (embedded/minimal-image maintenance, script portability); the relevant_experience field plausibly identifies the audience (Unix systems engineers maintaining ed/sed scripts).

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh writes exactly 0 initially, then unconditionally overwrites reward.txt with either '1' (rc==0) or '0' (rc!=0) based solely on pytest's exit code; every reachable path writes exactly 0 or 1, with no fractional or weighted scoring anywhere in the verifier.

task_security.explanation: No credential access, no exfiltration, no obfuscation. The guardcheck probes intentionally attempt subprocess/exec/ctypes usage purely to test the anti-cheat guard, which is the guard's own documented purpose. One case reads /etc/hostname via ed's 'r' command, which is benign (compared identically between reference and candidate, no external transmission).

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh invokes pytest with --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json directly against test_outputs.py, covering its 24 discrete tests (22 case-family tests plus the two guard/package tests), matching the standard CTRF pattern exactly.

outcome_verified.explanation: Tests only check final stdout, exit status, and resulting files against a live GNU ed run; instructions describe required behavior/output, not an implementation approach. No process-level constraints on how the agent must implement pyed.

solution_quality.explanation: solve.sh only copies pre-written solution/pyed/ed.py and posixre.py (each far over 20 lines) rather than inlining them as heredocs, matching the guidance to keep large files separate. The files themselves demonstrate genuine, non-trivial computation (a full editor engine and regex matcher), not a hardcoded answer.

category_and_tags.explanation: category='Software' and subcategory='Languages' reasonably fit a task about implementing a command-language interpreter and its own regex dialect. Tags (gnu-ed, line-editor, posix-regex, undo, reimplementation) are specific and descriptive, not generic.

environment_hygiene.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (README, docs, pyed stub); tests/ and solution/ are excluded via .dockerignore and never copied. tests/Dockerfile installs its own test-only deps (ed, pytest, pytest-json-ctrf) at build time, not in test.sh. Apt installs in both Dockerfiles are unpinned (correct per guidance) and followed by rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* cleanup, preceded by apt-get update.

no_extraneous_files.explanation: Every file inspected is referenced by a Dockerfile, the instruction, solve.sh, or the test harness (roster.json/fixtures.json cross-checked against the *.jsonl case files and found perfectly consistent, with fixture and total counts matching exactly). No leftover, backup, or unused files were found; the only hidden file is the standard .dockerignore.

essential_difficulty.explanation: The byte-exact output requirement is intrinsic to faithfully cloning GNU ed's documented behavior (e.g. the 'l' command's escaping rules, diagnostic messages), not an arbitrary formatting overlay bolted onto an otherwise different task. Failures would stem from misunderstanding ed's genuine semantics (current-address rules, undo, leftmost-longest matching), not clerical precision.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: The agent image ships no ed binary and has no network at solve time (agent network_mode=no-network), preventing trivial delegation. The guard.py launcher uses sys.addaudithook and a meta_path Warden to block subprocess/exec/fork/ctypes and non-stdlib/non-delivered imports, verified against five probe programs (launcher.py, exec_launcher.py, vendored.py, native.py, plain.py). test_delivered_package_is_standard_library_python additionally scans all delivered files for binary/native content and disallowed imports via AST, closing the loophole of dropping a compiled .so under /app. Ground truth is produced live from the verifier's own root-only /usr/bin/ed, never exposed to the agent.

instruction_concision.explanation: instruction.md is dense but purely descriptive of required behavior (uses absolute paths /app/pyed/ed.py, /app/docs/ed.txt; backticks for commands/paths; no headings, roleplay, or step-by-step procedure). It does not hint at implementation approach (no mention of linked lists, undo stacks, etc.).

do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: instruction.md contains no 'do not modify/preserve/leave unchanged' constraint naming a concrete artifact; its behavioral constraints (stdlib-only, no subprocess, no native code) are enforced by the guard/launcher and delivered-package tests but are not 'do-not-modify-a-file' constraints in the sense this criterion targets.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The task's expected output is plain stdout/file content matching GNU ed's behavior, not a structured schema like JSON/CSV/API response, so no normative schema documentation is needed.

functional_verification.explanation: The core verification (check()) executes both GNU ed and the candidate on 1644 real command scripts and diffs stdout/exit-status/files. The only string/AST-based checks (test_delivered_package_is_standard_library_python) validate the 'stdlib-only, no native code' constraint, which cannot be checked by execution alone and is a legitimate complement, not a substitute, for behavioral testing.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: Base images pinned by sha256 digest; pytest and pytest-json-ctrf pinned to exact versions; apt-get ed is intentionally left unpinned per guidance (apt mirrors only carry current point releases). No live/mutable network services are used at verify time (network_mode=no-network for both agent and verifier).

test_instruction_alignment.explanation: Every requirement in instruction.md (options -E/-l/-p/-q/-r/-s and no others, address forms, BRE/ERE with GNU escapes, leftmost-longest matching, all other commands/suffixes/global/undo/marks/G/V, error '?' + stop-on-regular-file/continue-on-pipe behavior) is covered by a corresponding case family or the launcher/package tests. Verified absence of excluded features (h/H commands, -G/-v options, '!' usage) in the corpus, matching the instruction's stated exceptions.

separate_verifier_configured.explanation: All verifier inputs (case corpus, guard/guardcheck/guardvendor, GNU ed binary, pytest/ctrf tooling) are baked into tests/Dockerfile; nothing is read from undeclared agent-container paths. No runtime pip/apt installs occur in test.sh. There are no shared assets duplicated between environment/ and tests/ that could drift.

solution_explanation_quality.explanation: solution_explanation accurately describes the two-file approach (posixre.py for BRE/ERE parsing and exhaustive leftmost-longest matching; ed.py for the circular line-list/undo-stack port) and is fully consistent with the actual solution files inspected.

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: Candidate code always runs via setpriv --reuid=65534 (nobody), never as root, and never in-process inside pytest (always via subprocess.Popen). /logs/verifier and /tests are chmod 700 and the reference ed binary is chmod 700 before any candidate code runs. Reward is derived by root (test.sh) purely from pytest's exit code. The audit-hook guard blocks fork/exec/spawn outright, closing the double-fork-daemon attack this criterion targets; timeouts kill the whole process group via killpg with start_new_session=True.

difficulty_explanation_quality.explanation: difficulty_explanation concretely enumerates the specific hard sub-problems (current-address rules, undo-of-undo, global active-list semantics, interactive G/V, leftmost-longest POSIX matching, error/exit-status nuances) and explains why an engineer working from memory would get specific details wrong. It also clarifies the corpus is synthetically generated from the grammar rather than an external corpus, addressing the data-realism requirement. The real-world audience is covered via the closely related relevant_experience field rather than embedded verbatim in difficulty_explanation, a minor stylistic gap.

verification_explanation_quality.explanation: verification_explanation accurately and specifically describes the verifier's mechanics (roster/fixture self-check, live GNU ed oracle per case, root-only ed binary, unprivileged launcher-wrapped candidate run, byte-for-byte/exit-status/file comparison, five guard probes, delivered-package stdlib/text check), all of which match what was found in test_outputs.py and guard.py.

[correct_reference_solution] Major
  [part 1 of 10] The reference is installed at the required path and implements the requested option parsing, alternation direction, leftmost-longest selection, and standard-input reading for interactive globals. Three reachable documented cases nevertheless diverge: setting a filename prints output that `f FILE` must not print; an unmarked address is treated as address zero; and a basic regular expression the manual expressly defines as literal is rejected. The latter can change output, exit status, and whether a file is written.

  [part 2 of 10] The reference distinguishes regular-file and pipe stdin, implements the missing-startup-file branch, and routes command errors through the required stdout notification. Its global substitution loop, however, passes each unconsumed suffix of a line to a new regex search. Word-boundary assertions then see that suffix as the beginning of a word rather than retaining their position in the addressed line. This changes both substitution output and, in some cases, whether a command succeeds.

  [part 3 of 10] The address, option, comment and prompt paths in this part implement their stated rules. A boundary between the join and undo rules does not: a one-line join correctly leaves the buffer unchanged, but discards the undo history of the preceding modification. A subsequent u therefore fails instead of undoing that modification.

  [part 4 of 10] Address offsets, bidirectional searches, empty-pattern reuse and the examined BRE boundaries follow the contract. An unset mark is mishandled specifically in an empty buffer: the reference converts it to address zero, so a command that should fail instead prints a value and exits successfully.

  [part 5 of 10] The reference implements much of the specified regexp and command parsing, but three ordinary, contract-valid regexp boundaries produce different editing results: a leading hyphen in a bracket expression becomes a range, extended-regexp anchors are applied in the middle of expressions, and an interval escape at the start of a basic regexp is rejected rather than matched literally. O85 and O86 describe the same last defect.

  [part 6 of 10] The listed command, suffix, edit, and global-command obligations have corresponding reference paths, including their principal boundary branches. A separate empty-buffer address boundary fails: resolving an unset mark produces the valid append address zero instead of an address error. This changes both output and exit status for a regular-file command script.

  [part 7 of 10] The reference implements the global-list, insertion, joining, marking, and printing paths examined here. Its move-command destination check misses one inclusive boundary: the last line of the moved range is a destination within that range, but the reference accepts it. A short valid pipe-fed script therefore differs in both stdout and exit-success status.

  [part 8 of 10] The prompt, quit, read, copy, inverse-global, and write paths implement the listed ordinary branches. Undo has a reachable boundary defect: a global command discards the previous undo history before establishing that it modified the buffer. A nonmatching global command therefore prevents u from undoing the actual last buffer-modifying command, contradicting the manual's definition.

  [part 9 of 10] The reference implements the ordinary x/y, z, addressing, and substitution-suffix paths, but two reachable substitution boundaries contradict the manual. Successful substitution yanks the old line rather than the last modified line. A nonfinal global-list substitution lacking its final delimiter does not receive the required error disposition and can loop after the command buffer ends. Separately, an unsuccessful substitution destroys an earlier command's undo history even though it modified nothing.

     final delimiter and is not last because `p` follows, a form the manual expressly forbids.
     In extract_replacement, after collecting `b`, the first newline is not accepted as the end
     because isglobal is true and more text remains (solution lines 545-547); it appends that
     newline and `p` to rbuf, stopping only at the final newline. Thus rbuf is `b\np`,
     substitution replaces `a` with two lines `b` and `p`, and its omitted-delimiter implicit
     print emits `p\n`. Flip: GNU ed must reject the forbidden command form with `?\n` under the
     contract rule, rather than silently mutate the buffer and print `p\n`.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:905-910, solution/pyed/ed.py:545-562,
     solution/pyed/ed.py:1060-1081, solution/pyed/ed.py:1313-1352

53. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- dependency enforcement mismatch
   The runtime import guard classifies site-packages beneath the Python standard-library
   directory as standard-library code.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: A delivered program can use the standard-library `importlib` API to dynamically
     import an installed non-standard-library package, such as verifier-installed `pytest`; a
     syntactic `import importlib` passes the source audit. Flip: In the verifier image, an
     origin below `/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/` begins with the
     `/usr/local/lib/python3.13` standard-library prefix, so check_origin does not stop the
     import and a GNU-equivalent implementation using that dependency could pass the output
     comparisons despite breaking the build restriction. This requires deliberately exploiting
     the guard's path test rather than an ordinary way to implement ed.
   Where to look: tests/Dockerfile:3-4, tests/guard.py:20-22, tests/guard.py:46-51,
     tests/test_outputs.py:207-217

54. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   No shown case directly distinguishes y preserving current from y setting current to the last
   yanked line.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: with fixture f_01, run `1y
     .p
     `; current initially is 10, so GNU ed prints `kappa ten`, while an implementation that
     makes y set current to 1 prints `alpha one`. Flip: the shown focused yank cases give x an
     explicit address or otherwise do not directly assert current immediately after y. Reach
     through the unseen mixed-script files is unverified, so this is advisory.
   Where to look: tests/cases/delete_join_move_copy.jsonl:13-15,
     environment/app/docs/ed.txt:823-826

55. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The shown cut-buffer cases never distinguish replacement by a second y from retaining or
   accumulating the first yank.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: on fixture f_12 (`a\nb\n`), run `1y
     2y
     0x
     ,p
     Q
     `. The second y must replace the cut buffer with `b`, yielding printed lines `b`, `a`, `b`;
     retaining the first yank inserts `a` instead. Flip: the focused yank cases at lines 13-24
     contain no successive y commands. Whether an unseen mixed-script case supplies this
     distinction is unverified.
   Where to look: tests/cases/delete_join_move_copy.jsonl:13-24,
     environment/app/docs/ed.txt:823-826

56. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The shown comment checks require an address, leaving address-free comments unexercised.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: on fixture f_12, `# ignored
     .=
     ` must ignore the first line and print `2`. Flip: a parser that accepts # only after
     parsing an address clears the shown `1,2#comment` and `1;# ignored` cases but emits `?` for
     this input. The unseen mixed-script cases were not available to check for this form.
   Where to look: tests/cases/print_list_number.jsonl:10, tests/cases/addresses.jsonl:53,
     environment/app/docs/ed.txt:852-856

57. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   No shown case checks a numeric COUNT on the repeat-substitution form.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: on two lines `aaa\naaa\n`, run `1s/a/X/`, `2s2`, `2p`, `Q`. Flip: a repeat parser
     that accepts `s` but not `s2` passes the shown repeat cases and fails this legal input, for
     which the second line's second `a` must be replaced. The NOT SHOWN mixed-script files
     prevent confirming absence across the full corpus.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:923-929, tests/cases/substitute.jsonl:12-13,
     tests/cases/substitute.jsonl:38-39

58. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The shown `sg` case does not test the required reset of a previous numeric COUNT.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: on `aaa\naaa\n`, run `1s/a/X/2`, `2sg`, `2p`, `Q`. Flip: an implementation that
     toggles `g` but retains COUNT 2 differs from GNU ed's count-reset behavior;
     substitute.jsonl:38 instead toggles a previously global, uncounted substitution. Coverage
     in mixed_scripts_6–8 is unverified.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:928-931, tests/cases/substitute.jsonl:38

59. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The shown repeat-substitution examples never observe whether `sp` toggles an existing print
   suffix off.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: on `aa\naa\n`, run `1s/a/X/p`, `2sp`, `2p`, `Q`. Flip: a repeat implementation that
     always enables printing emits an extra line on `2sp`, whereas toggling disables that print.
     The shown substitute family tests repeat `g` and `r`, not this toggle; mixed_scripts_6–8
     are unverified.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:928-932, tests/cases/substitute.jsonl:38-39

60. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The shown `sr` case tests a later search but not the condition that the search must follow
   the substitution.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: with `alpha\nbeta\n`, search `/b/`, then execute `1s/a/X/`, `2sr`, `2p`, `Q`. Flip:
     an implementation that always chooses the last search pattern for `sr`, regardless of its
     age, substitutes `b` rather than the previous substitution's `a`. substitute.jsonl:39 puts
     its search after the substitution; mixed_scripts_6–8 are unverified.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:931-934, tests/cases/substitute.jsonl:39

61. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The visible corpus lacks cases for raw BRE brace/angle literals and for a general ordinary
   escaped literal, leaving a BRE translator that delegates those forms to Python regex behavior
   insufficiently checked.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: unverified -- inspection of the displayed tests/cases/regex.jsonl lines 1-42 finds
     literal-parenthesis coverage (line 40), escaped `\t`/`\'` coverage (lines 14 and 38-39),
     and interval syntax, but no command containing raw `{`, `}`, `<`, `>`, or an ordinary
     unsupported escape such as `\q`; mixed_scripts_6-8 are NOT SHOWN. Flip: a plausible
     translator that passes unrecognized `\q` to Python re (which rejects it) and fails to quote
     raw braces would differ from GNU ed on a legal script such as `a\nq\n.\ng/\q/p\nQ\n`, or on
     input containing `{2}` with `g/{2}/p`; the verifier's tuple comparison at
     tests/test_outputs.py:133-143 would fail if such a case were added. The shown suite cannot
     establish that the hidden mixed-script files do not already cover this, so this is Minor
     rather than a confirmed Major.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:460-469, tests/cases/regex.jsonl:14,
     tests/cases/regex.jsonl:29-42, tests/test_outputs.py:128-143

62. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The visible corpus does not test rejection of a nonblank first g COMMAND-LIST command
   deferred to the next physical line.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: unverified -- the shown global corpus (tests/cases/global_commands.jsonl:1-25) has
     same-line first commands or a legal blank list, but no g/a/ followed by a nonblank first
     command. A cheap contract-legal distinguishing script on a buffer containing two a lines is
     `g/a/\nd\n,p\n`: GNU treats the empty list as p for each match, then executes one top-level
     d; an implementation that permits the deferred d as the global list deletes both matches.
     Flip: stdout, final snapshot, and potentially status differ under check(), which compares
     the complete run tuple at tests/test_outputs.py:132-143. This is Minor because
     mixed_scripts_6-8 are not shown and may cover it.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:668-677, tests/cases/global_commands.jsonl:1-25,
     tests/test_outputs.py:128-143

63. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   No visible global-command case establishes that file commands such as w remain legal members
   of a g COMMAND-LIST.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: unverified -- the shown dedicated global corpus uses p, s, d, m, t, j, a, n, k and
     nested-command errors, but not `w` as the list command. A plausible partial implementation
     can whitelist only these encountered commands and reject w. The cheap legal distinguisher
     is `g/a/w out\n` with a buffer having an a line: GNU creates out from each matching
     execution, whereas the partial implementation emits ? and leaves no out. Flip: check()
     compares both stdout and snapshot(path), including out, at tests/test_outputs.py:132-143.
     This remains Minor because the three unshown mixed-script files may contain this
     combination.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:668-672, tests/cases/global_commands.jsonl:1-25,
     tests/test_outputs.py:84-93, tests/test_outputs.py:128-143

64. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The visible interactive-global cases never apply an explicit address range to G, leaving its
   required address scoping unexercised.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: unverified -- all shown G invocations are unaddressed (`G/a/`, `G/o/`, etc.) in
     tests/cases/interactive_global.jsonl:1-11. A plausible implementation can always scan the
     entire buffer for G while correctly handling its interaction and I suffix. The cheap legal
     distinguishing input is a three-line buffer `a\nx\na\n` and `2,2G/a/\np\n\n`: GNU has no
     selected line and prints nothing, while the incorrect full-buffer implementation processes
     and prints both a lines. Flip: stdout differs in check()'s tuple comparison at
     tests/test_outputs.py:132-143. This is Minor because mixed_scripts_6-8 are not shown.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/ed.txt:679-686,
     tests/cases/interactive_global.jsonl:1-11, tests/test_outputs.py:128-143

fields.label: Prompt Check
fields.description:
I reviewed my prompt (instruction.md) and:

  • Ensured it does not list an excessive number of requirements (20+)
  • Made it sound natural and human
  • Removed any unnecessary hints and verified it does not reveal the solution
fields.checkboxLabel: I confirm that the above is true and understand that if not, the submission is subject to rejection.

fields.label: Difficulty check results

fields.label: Quality Judge Panel Feedback
fields.description:
After initial submission, you will be provided with detailed feedback along 5 axes, each answering a core question about your task:

  1. Coherent Contracts: Can a candidate determine every rule used to grade the task?
  2. Correct Reference Solution: Does the reference satisfy the documented task?
  3. Protected Ground Truth: Can candidate code obtain or control the answer the grader trusts?
  4. Sound Verifier: Does grading reject wrong solutions and accept contract-valid ones?
  5. Deterministic Execution: Does the same submission receive stable grading on repeated runs?

Keep these in mind when reviewing this feedback, and refer to the guidelines for more details on this feedback.

fields.label: Oracle / NOP validation
fields.description: Result of running your reference solution three times and an empty solution once in your task's environment. If your image did not build, the failing Dockerfile step and its output are quoted here. Fix the task, rebuild both images locally on a fresh checkout, and resubmit.
